# SBML model authoring

For an account-backed workspace, fetch an exact BioModels artifact with authenticated MCP and place it in the workspace by opaque resource ID. Preserve the original SBML bytes and checksum. For local/offline work, pin the downloaded file and checksum in the local project instead. Build a thin `TelluriumSBMLBioModule` integration around the source; do not manually rewrite equations or parameters to make execution easier.

Inspect the installed `TelluriumSBMLBioModule` contract before authoring its
subclass. Its public constructor accepts `model_path` and optional
`integration_step`; declare adapter behavior with the supported class metadata
such as `_OBSERVABLES`, `_PARAMETER_INPUTS`, `_INITIAL_CONDITION_INPUTS`,
`_MULTIPLIER_INPUTS`, output aliases, and visualization hooks. Do not invent
constructor keywords, assume a manifest declaration configures the Python
adapter, or hide an unsupported source perturbation behind an approximate
parameter change.

Distinguish global SBML parameters from reaction-local kinetic-law parameters.
Before exposing any parameter, prove the native runtime can address that exact
identifier. A local XML ID such as `V1` does not become a global RoadRunner
selection merely because it appears in the source. When the requested value is
already immutable in the source and cannot be addressed, keep it unexposed; an
upstream component may validate a locked reference value but must not claim it
mutated the SBML.

Document species/parameter mappings, public ports, units, event semantics, solver assumptions, initialization, and supported perturbations in the model documentation when useful. Add tests for source parsing, declared inputs/outputs, units, representative trajectories, conservation or invariant checks where scientifically applicable, and failure behavior. Pin literature or database evidence separately. Report solver or model limitations in caveats.

Treat missing source units as missing metadata. Preserve the source convention
or require an explicit, cited conversion; do not relabel an unannotated SBML
quantity as nM, nM/minute, or another physical unit. When requested, native-runtime parity can
execute an independent reference path against the immutable source and compare
the resulting trajectory. A value asserted by the adapter under test is not an
independent parity result.

Verify the physical/evaluation time basis with an executed source trajectory.
Do not equate requested minutes with raw SBML time units when the source omits a
complete time-unit declaration. If the intended-use protocol defines a
conversion, record it explicitly, apply it consistently to run duration,
sampling, peak times, and plots, and retain both raw source time and reported
time semantics.

Keep the source-faithful time-course adapter on its supported temporal hook. Any
new finite preprocessor uses `execute(inputs, *, context)` with the imported enum
member `ExecutionPolicy.ONCE_BEFORE_RUN`; never use the invalid quoted uppercase
string `"ONCE_BEFORE_RUN"`.




Scientific qualification is removed. Legacy profile metadata is descriptive. Documents, evidence, reference fixtures and visualizations are not platform prerequisites. Preserve real execution errors, scoped authorization and files. File-only work needs no chart. For 0.0.38+, report inner failures with ExecutionOutcome through report_execution_outcome.
